lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Add a target-role label or summary near the name.
items.because: A quick reader has to infer your intended direction from the rest of the page.

items.says: Consider whether Experience should lead instead of Education for roles that value your work experience more.
items.because: Education first is reasonable while you are pursuing the M.S., but may not be the strongest order for every target role.

items.says: Put Experience in reverse chronological order.
items.because: The internship ending in May 2025 appears after the role ending in July 2024.

items.says: Prioritize the strongest three or four internship bullets.
items.because: Six bullets is a lot for an internship, especially when several cover related training experiments.

items.says: Expand and refocus the brief Skills section around relevant demonstrated capabilities.
items.because: Recruiters and ATS should be able to find skills relevant to the target roles more easily.

items.says: Make the code link lead directly to relevant work if it is important to your candidacy.
items.because: A general landing page may be less useful.

items.says: Keep the expected completion date and status unambiguous and current.
Clarify whether you owned the dashboards, the on-call rotation, or both.
items.because: The scope of ownership is not fully clear.

items.says: Add an outcome to the ownership bullet.
items.because: Without one, it may be less valuable than the more measurable work.

items.says: Clarify how the regression checks shortened the release cycle.
items.because: The sentence attributes the entire improvement to the checks without showing what else changed.

items.says: Separate or trim the migration bullet’s multiple accomplishments and responsibilities.
items.because: It combines a migration, logging rewrite, onboarding, on-call work, and a dispatch outcome.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution.
items.because: The bullet lists several kinds of work without making your part distinct.

items.says: Clarify what produced the dispatch outcome.
items.because: The result sounds attributable to every item in the list.

items.says: Clarify what screening 800+ sensor signals per case means in the workflow.
Clarify whether the backlog reduction was attributable to the launched system.
items.because: Other changes during the eight weeks could have contributed.

items.says: Make the specialized terms understandable to the intended readers.
items.because: “Domain adapter” and “assistant-only loss masking” may be opaque to some readers.

items.says: Clarify the evaluation setup and comparison.
items.because: A technical reviewer needs enough context for the accuracy result.

items.says: Clarify the workload and measurement setup for the dynamic-batching result.
items.because: “Single-request” and “dynamic batching” may appear contradictory.

items.says: Reduce or better justify the procedural detail in the GRPO latency bullet.
items.because: The sentence is method-heavy for a 5% result.

items.says: State the comparison baseline and whether quality measures changed.
items.because: The latency gain lacks that context.

items.says: Make the grammatical subject and source of the result unmistakable.
Provide evidence that single-rollout sampling stabilized training or say what improved.
items.because: The résumé does not state how you know it had that effect.

items.says: Add a concrete indication of the runbook’s use or effect if available.
items.because: Otherwise, the claim should stay limited to what the reviewers adopted.

items.says: Describe your project role and scope more clearly than “Owner.”
items.because: “Owner” is less informative.

items.says: Distinguish current project work from completed results.
items.because: The project is marked ongoing.

items.says: Substantiate or remove the broad AI-first practices claim.
items.because: It gives no concrete action, measure, or example of adoption or improved outcomes.

items.says: The claimed 50% latency reduction is incorrect.
items.because: Going from 900 ms to 600 ms is roughly a 33% reduction.

items.says: Check that the latency baseline and measured result are comparable.
The task-completion gain is stated as 12% rather than 12 percentage points.
items.because: The rate rose from 71% to 83%, which is not a 12% relative increase.

items.says: Identify the benchmark conditions briefly if needed.
items.because: They would make the result more credible.

items.says: Make the contribution and its adoption clear without relying on “upstreamed.”
items.because: Some recruiters may not understand the term.

items.says: Specify what variables the Kendall correlation relates.
items.because: Otherwise the statistic can sound detached from its meaning.

items.says: Explain what the 400+ trials represent.
items.because: That context gives the statistic meaning.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to identifying the defects.
Add the practical effect of the upstream fixes if available.
Consider replacing Git with a more target-relevant capability or tool.
items.because: Git may be less valuable in this list.

items.says: Reorganize the ML & Agents skills by type.
items.because: The category mixes methods, concepts, and infrastructure tools, and Kubernetes does not naturally fit under it.

items.says: Consider surfacing demonstrated work in serving, evaluation, CI, monitoring, or deployment.
items.because: Those capabilities appear in the experience but are not visible in the skills list.
